description: Platform-level CRITERION and CONTRACT knowledge objects. These are the obligations every task-kit consumer inherits; they are deliberately kept in one seed file so the tolerance policy has exactly one machine-readable home.

criteria.title: Error above 15 % against experiment/reference is unacceptable
criteria.metric: relative error vs experiment or reference solution

criteria.title: Report target: key quantity within 3 % of the benchmark

contracts.title: Task-kit consumption contract v1
contracts.scope: Every task dispatched with an anchor must consume the anchor's KO graph before producing results, and must emit results in the same six-form vocabulary.
obligations: Resolve the anchor slug to a KO; if absent, the task creates it rather than writing free text.
State the criterion the result is judged by (id of a CRITERION KO), not an ad-hoc tolerance.
Attach at least one EVIDENCE KO per reported key quantity, with a re-runnable command and an artefact path.
Declare an evidence grade and keep the mechanically-derived grade reachable for audit (declared vs mechanical may not silently diverge).
File every defect found as a DEFECT KO linked to the case it was found in, so negative knowledge survives the mission.
contracts.tolerance_policy: CRITERION-PLATFORM-15PCT is a hard floor; CRITERION-PLATFORM-3PCT is the reporting target. A result between the two must be reported as an honest partial PASS, never as PASS.
contracts.consumer: any agent (task-kit dispatcher, reviewer, or downstream solver repo) reading the index

contracts.title: Evidence grading contract v1
contracts.scope: Rules for assigning REAL/MOCK/STUB/WITHHELD/NOT_SUPPORTED to a reported capability.
obligations: REAL requires a re-runnable artefact whose numbers can be recomputed offline; a narrative claim alone is not REAL.
MOCK requires the artefact to say which values are hard-coded or randomised.
WITHHELD is used when the artefact referenced by a document does not exist or cannot be parsed; it is not a synonym for 'not yet done'.
Downgrading a declared grade is always allowed and never requires owner approval; upgrading does.
contracts.tolerance_policy: declared_grade vs mechanical_grade divergence is a reportable defect, not a style issue
